insights.insight: 88,762 cryptographically verified receipts have been logged against $4.71M in confirmed GMV — this is deterministic purchase proof, not modeled audience inference, running at a structural pace of ~457 receipts per day.

Every receipt in the Crinkl protocol confirms a completed transaction at a named retailer; the gap between this and probabilistic ad targeting (CPM-based inference from site visits) is the difference between knowing a purchase happened and guessing it might.

The 7-day rolling GMV has closed between $94K and $102K across nine of the last ten pre-rollover windows, establishing a consistent weekly verified-spend floor that brands can model against for reach planning.

The 14-day brand leaderboard — Walmart (334 receipts), Kroger (164), Publix (128), Costco (126), Home Depot (60) — confirms the protocol captures both grocery and home-improvement spend, giving CPG and durables brands overlapping verified audience pools.

Post-rollover GMV floors have held in the $82K–$86K range across all ten measured UTC midnight resets, regardless of how large the rollover drop is — this is a demand-consistency signal, not a one-time spike artifact.

Whole Foods Market appeared in the brand leaderboard for the first time on 2026-10-09 and Aldi crossed the visibility threshold on 2026-10-06, suggesting the verified-receipt network is extending into premium and value grocery simultaneously — category breadth is widening.
